kids: Watch the downtown Christmas tree light up at 6:45 PM

about: The City of Inverness calls Small Town Rockin' Christmas a free holiday celebration in Downtown Inverness and the kickoff to its 12 Days of Christmas event series, so it is the first stop for families planning December in town.
The city lists the evening as running from 5 to 9 PM on the Square, with the downtown Christmas tree lighting at 6:45 PM and stage performances from 7 to 9 PM.
The music lineup named by the city includes the Salvation Army Band, the Hernando Harmonizers and A Rockin' Blue Christmas with Johnny Rogers, who bring Christmas favorites to the stage.
Families can visit with Santa Claus at the Old Historic Courthouse Museum.
The city presents the event in partnership with the Rotary Club of Downtown Inverness. Admission is free.

Later events in the series include Movie Night at Liberty Park on December 4, Light Up Liberty on December 5, the Inverness Christmas Parade on December 12 and Small Town Saturday Night on December 19.
The city lists the Old Historic Courthouse Museum as the place where families visit Santa Claus during the celebration.
With the stage music running from 7 to 9 PM after the 6:45 PM tree lighting, families with younger children can catch the lighting first and head home early, or stay for the full concert.
faq: When is Small Town Rockin' Christmas in 2026?
Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 5 to 9 PM in Downtown Inverness on the Square.

Yes. The City of Inverness lists it as a free event.
When does the Christmas tree get lit?
The City of Inverness lists the lighting of the Downtown Christmas tree at 6:45 PM, before the live stage performances begin at 7 PM.
Who performs?
The Salvation Army Band, the Hernando Harmonizers and A Rockin' Blue Christmas with Johnny Rogers, with stage performances from 7 to 9 PM.
Where can kids meet Santa?
Families can visit Santa Claus at the Old Historic Courthouse Museum.
Who presents the event?
The City of Inverness presents it in partnership with the Rotary Club of Downtown Inverness.

See the Christmas tree and lamp posts light up

about: The City of Inverness describes Light Up Liberty as its annual free holiday celebration for the whole family, held at Liberty Park.
The program counts down to the lighting of the Christmas tree and the decorated lamp posts, and the city lists the Holiday Boat Parade, hosted by Bluewater Drafting, starting at 5:45 PM.
Between the parade and the lighting, families can take part in holiday crafts and activities and visit with Santa Claus.
Local food vendors serve dinner at the park, and a special holiday market offers unique gifts and seasonal finds for shoppers.
The city lists the event on its calendar from 5 to 8 PM and carries a dedicated City Events page named Light Up Liberty.
The week before, Small Town Rockin' Christmas lights the downtown tree on the Square, and Movie Night at Liberty Park shows The Polar Express the night before this event on December 4.

The Inverness city calendar files Light Up Liberty under its Parks, Recreations, Events and Cultural Art category, alongside other seasonal gatherings such as Small Town Saturday Night on December 19.
Because the event runs only three hours, families who want the boat parade should plan to be at the water before the 5:45 PM start and stay for the tree and lamp post countdown afterward.
The Inverness Christmas Parade follows a week later on December 12, so Light Up Liberty works well as the waterfront half of a two weekend December plan.
Families arriving for the 5:45 PM Holiday Boat Parade should plan to be at the park before the boats begin, since the lighting countdown follows the parade.
The special holiday market is a good stop for early gift shopping, since the city says it features unique gifts and seasonal finds alongside the food vendors.
faq: When is Light Up Liberty in 2026?
Light Up Liberty takes place on Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 5 to 8 PM at Liberty Park in Inverness, according to the City of Inverness calendar.
Does it cost anything?
No. The City of Inverness calls Light Up Liberty a free holiday celebration for the whole family.
When does the boat parade start?
The Holiday Boat Parade, hosted by Bluewater Drafting, begins at 5:45 PM.

Yes. The city lists a visit with Santa Claus along with holiday crafts and activities.
Is there food?
Yes. The city says local food vendors will be on site, and a special holiday market offers unique gifts and seasonal finds for those who want to shop.
What lights up at the end of the countdown?
The Christmas tree and the decorated lamp posts at Liberty Park.
Who hosts the boat parade?
Bluewater Drafting hosts the Holiday Boat Parade, which begins at 5:45 PM.

about: The City of Inverness Parks and Recreation hosts a free showing of The Polar Express (2004) at Liberty Park on Friday, December 4, 2026, beginning at approximately 6 PM.
The city asks guests to bring blankets, lawn chairs and picnic baskets and to settle in for a family friendly evening under the stars.
Food and other vendors are available on site, and the city lists admission as free.
The film follows a young boy who takes a magical Christmas Eve trip to the North Pole on the Polar Express, learning about friendship, bravery and the spirit of Christmas.
Liberty Park is also the home of Light Up Liberty on Saturday, December 5, so families can return the next evening for the tree lighting and boat parade.
The movie night is part of the city's holiday lineup that begins with Small Town Rockin' Christmas on November 28 and continues with the Christmas Parade on December 12.
The city posted the Polar Express announcement on November 17 along with its other holiday events, so families can plan the whole season from the City of Inverness news page.
The city asks guests to bring their own picnic baskets, blankets and lawn chairs, which is the best way to get comfortable on the lawn once the film starts at about 6 PM.
The Polar Express was released in 2004 and tells the story of one boy's Christmas Eve journey, making it a long running family favorite for an outdoor night.
Because the showing begins at approximately 6 PM on a Friday, it falls the evening before the larger Saturday celebration at the same park.
The Inverness calendar lists this movie night under Parks and Recreation Events at Liberty Park at 6 PM on December 4.
faq: When is the Polar Express movie night in Inverness?
Friday, December 4, 2026, beginning at approximately 6 PM at Liberty Park.

kids: See floats, marching bands and Santa arrive
Spot manatees in Santa hats on Nature Coast themed floats
Spread out blankets and lawn chairs along the route
about: The Citrus County Chamber of Commerce produces the 2026 Inverness Christmas Parade, and the City of Inverness lists it on its official calendar for Saturday, December 12, 2026, at noon.
This year's theme is Nature Coast Christmas, which the chamber says celebrates what makes the corner of Florida special, from manatees in Santa hats to Christmas trees sparkling beside the springs.
The chamber promises creative floats, marching bands, familiar faces and the arrival of Santa, and describes it as a beloved Citrus County tradition.

The route enters W. Main Street near Dunkin' Donuts, travels east toward downtown and turns onto E. Grace Street just past Mama's Kuntry Kafe. It then continues toward HCA Florida Citrus Hospital and onto S. Line Avenue and W. Highland Boulevard, ending at Citrus High School.
Road closures are expected from about 10:45 AM until 2 PM. Main Street is closed from Hwy. 44 East to Montgomery Avenue, with detours along Montgomery Avenue and W. Highland Boulevard.
Alternate routes are listed for Gospel Island, Highlands South and Pleasant Grove Road residents, and the chamber can be reached at PR@citruscountychamber.com.
faq: When is the Inverness Christmas Parade in 2026?
Saturday, December 12, 2026, at noon in downtown Inverness.
What is the 2026 parade theme?
Nature Coast Christmas.
Where does the parade go?
It enters W. Main Street near Dunkin' Donuts, travels east and turns onto E. Grace Street, then follows S. Line Avenue and W. Highland Boulevard to Citrus High School.
When do roads close?
Road closures begin at about 10:45 AM and are expected to last until about 2 PM.
What should we bring to watch?
Blankets, lawn chairs, family and friends, and arrive early to find a good spot along the route.
Who organizes the parade?
The Citrus County Chamber of Commerce produces the parade, and you can reach the chamber at PR@citruscountychamber.com.
